checks.label: Because we have sinusoidal variation in time, the vertical component (magnitude times the sine of the angle it makes with the x axis) gives v(t): at every moment of the first screen's turn, and at every arm length on the third, the pen sits level with the arm's tip at the arm's length times the sine of its angle, and every drawn point of the wave is that height at its time

The length of the second hand represents the height or amplitude of the sine wave: at every arm length from 1 to 10 the arm is drawn that long on the circle, the wave over one turn reaches exactly that height and sinks to minus it, and the label on its peak reads amplitude and that length

The frequency indicates how many cycles exist in one second: at every setting from 1 to 50 turns a second each drawn wave is one turn of the arm, the time axis marks the end of the first and second turns at 1 ÷ f and 2 ÷ f seconds, so f waves fill one second, and the period bracket over the first wave reads 1 ÷ f
Low voltage supplies shall be 50 hertz: relabelled for 50 hertz, the time axis marks each turn at 20 ms and 40 ms, the period bracket reads 20 ms and the row works out 1 ÷ 50 = 0.02 s = 20 ms
360° = 2π radians: one turn is marked 2π, so f turns a second is 2πf radians a second, and the ω pill reads 2π × 50 = 314.16 rad/s at 50 Hz and 2π times the turns a second at every other setting

A(t) = Amax sin(ωt) = Amax sin(2πft): at 50 Hz every drawn point of the wave, read off the graph at its time t in seconds, equals sin(2π × 50 × t), and the arm points right again at the end of each turn, 20 ms and 40 ms

The terminal side of the angle intersects the circle at the point (x, y), which is equivalent to (cos t, sin t): at every start angle and time, arm B's tip is drawn at (cos θ, sin θ) times its length, its pen draws the sine, the switch traces arm A's across shadow, the cosine, and at a start angle of 90° that trace lies exactly on wave B

A start angle φ slides the whole wave left by φ ÷ ω: at every start angle from 0° to 360°, wave B at each drawn time is wave A a time φ ÷ ω later, the bracket from B's first peak to A's reads that slide, and at 90° it is a quarter period, 5 ms at 50 Hz

A level line between the peaks meets each wave twice: at every height from −10 to 10 each dot lies on the drawn wave and the line; at 5 the first two are at 1.67 ms and 8.33 ms (0.524 and 2.618 radians ÷ 314.16), and the wave first reaches −8.3 at 13.1 ms (π + 0.979 = 4.121 radians), with 16.9 ms next
